transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

Before replacing it, weak suction on a Shark upright is very often a blockage or overdue filter clean rather than a failed motor. Work through these with it unplugged:

1. Wash both filters
• Your NZ801UK has pre-motor foam/felt filters and a post-motor/HEPA filter.
• Remove them, rinse in cold water only (no detergent), squeeze out excess water, and leave them to dry fully for at least 24–48 hours.
• They must be completely dry before refitting — using damp filters can damage the vacuum and seriously reduce airflow.
• Even if they don’t look terrible, fine dust can clog them.

2. Check the brush roll and floorhead airway
• Remove hair, thread and fluff from around the brush roll and its ends. “Anti Hair Wrap” reduces wrapping but doesn’t prevent build-up entirely.
• Look underneath/behind the roller for packed dust or a blockage in the narrow airway leading up from the floorhead.
• Check that the roller spins freely and the floorhead flap/doors aren’t jammed.

3. Clear the hose, wand and main air path
• Detach the hose/wand and look through them towards a light. A compacted blockage can sit at bends, especially near the handle, the lower hose connection, or where the wand meets the main body.
• Use a broom handle carefully to push a blockage through; don’t use anything sharp that could puncture the hose.
• Check the inlet behind/under the bin as well — emptying the bin does not necessarily clear the passage into it.

4. Do a quick suction test to locate the issue
• With the bin fitted and filters in place, turn it on and test suction at the end of the hose with the floorhead disconnected.
• Strong suction at the hose but weak pickup from the floor: blockage/fault in the floorhead, brush roll, or lower hose.
• Weak suction at the hose too: filters, blockage in the main body, bin seal, or potentially the motor.

5. Check the bin and seals
• Make sure the bin is clicked fully into place and that its rubber seals/gaskets are clean, undamaged and seated properly.
• Check for cracks in the hose or loose connections; an air leak can make floor pickup poor.

6. Check the settings
• Ensure it is set for the surface you’re vacuuming. If the floorhead is sitting too high, crumbs may not be drawn in effectively; if it is too low on thick carpet it can restrict airflow.
• Make sure any suction-control slider on the handle is fully closed for maximum suction.

If suction remains poor after fully drying cleaned filters and clearing every air path, I would not buy a new machine yet. The NZ801UK was commonly sold with a long Shark guarantee (often 5 years, depending on registration/purchase date). Contact Shark UK support with the model and serial number; a replacement hose, floorhead or filter set may solve it, and some faults may be covered.

Did the checks. Suction is weak at the end of the hose too. Coin goes through the hose fine and the wand is clear. Brushroll has a bit of fluff but spins freely, and the bin seal looks fine. I've never washed the filters, didn't know they were there. The foam one is solid grey and the felt is caked with dust. No burning smell and it hasn't cut out. I'll wash them now.

That sounds very likely to be the cause. A solid-grey foam filter and dust-caked felt filter can restrict airflow enough to make suction poor everywhere, including at the hose.

• Rinse the foam and felt filters under cold running water only — no detergent.
• Gently squeeze them repeatedly until the water runs clear. Don’t wring the felt aggressively.
• Leave them somewhere warm with good airflow for at least 24 hours, preferably 48. They need to be completely dry right through before going back in.
• Do not run the vacuum without them or while they are damp.

While they’re drying, it is worth locating and checking/washing the post-motor/HEPA filter too, if your NZ801UK has its filter access flap. It is normally behind a separate cover/grille on the main unit, rather than beside the foam/felt filters. Rinse with cold water only and give it the same full drying time. Check the markings/manual on the filter cover if unsure.

Once everything is dry and refitted, test suction at the hose before using the floorhead. I’d expect a substantial improvement based on what you found.

If it is still weak after that:

1. Buy replacement foam/felt filters (and HEPA filter if applicable), especially if the existing ones remain stiff, misshapen, smell musty, or don’t rinse reasonably clean.
2. Recheck the air inlet directly behind the dust bin and the lower connection where the hose joins the machine — that is where compacted dust can hide despite a clear hose/wand.
3. If suction remains weak at the bare hose with clean, dry filters, the remaining possibilities are an internal blockage or an air leak/motor issue. But given the untouched filters, I would not consider replacing the cleaner until you’ve tested it after cleaning them.
